items.title: 56422_Leonard Phillips oral history interview
items.q: We opened up with Louis Armstrong's band. Lionel Hampton stayed up there two weeks. Tony Pastor. Cootie Williams. Jimmy Lunceford...

ctx.x: Yeah, he was in there with John. He got a band himself around '54. We just gigged. That was about three gigs. Doin' pretty good. The music was dying then. That's when it was goin' down, round about '54. Rock-and-Roll was comin' in like Faust. Rock-and-Roll and Rhythm-and-Blues. People wasn't carin' about no Jazz too much then.

Then after that, Al Dunn got a band together, and went up to the Music Hall. Stayed up there about four months. We was the house band there. We opened up with Louis Armstrong's band. Lionel Hampton stayed up there two weeks. Tony Pastor. Cootie Williams. Jimmy Lunceford...
